name: Dan "Kilo" Sallis

summary.text: Dan "Kilo" Sallis is a Libertarian Party candidate for U.S. House in Colorado's 7th District, running as a small business owner (CEO of Cynch) who has never held public office.
He lives in the Ken Caryl area of Jefferson County and has called the 7th District home since 1967, when his family moved to Littleton.
He holds a degree from the University of Colorado Denver and says his campaign accepts no political contributions of any kind.

experience.text: Small business owner; CEO of Cynch.
B.A./degree from the University of Colorado Denver.

positions.quote: Healthcare Freedom with reduced costs through deregulation & tort reform
positions.note: Listed as one of his top three priorities; his campaign site elaborates that he supports repealing ACA mandates and relying on free-market competition instead of expanded government coverage.

positions.quote: Yes, more public land should be made available for extraction. Energy independence is a top national security priority.
positions.note: His campaign site similarly opposes 'top-down federal energy mandates' and 'federal fracking bans,' while saying oil, gas, and renewables should all compete.

positions.source_title: Colorado U.S. House District 7 candidate Q&A - The Denver Post
positions.quote: I support securing the border while dramatically expanding legal pathways so people can come here to work, not sneak in.
positions.note: Puts expanding legal immigration pathways first rather than treating deportation of unauthorized immigrants as the top priority.

research_notes: Sallis's Ballotpedia page is a stub with no Candidate Connection survey. He is one of only two CD-7 candidates (with Pettersen) who answered the Denver Post's 2026 candidate questionnaire, which gave strong, dated material. His own campaign site (dankilo.com) elaborates on several of the same positions in more detail but carries no page dates, so those citations use the access date. No sourced position found on abortion beyond the inferred one above, nor on the Colorado ballot measures (Amendments 81-87, Propositions 132-137) despite checking his site's Issues page, which does not mention them by name. Build review 2026-10-14: removed inferred position(s) on fentanyl-penalties, abortion-legal; the source states a general principle and does not name that policy area.
